newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos seeks monthly reports on corruption in govt.
newsitem.headline: Ramos seeks monthly reports on corruption in govt.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos ordered all government departments and agencies on Saturday to submit monthly progress reports on their fight against corruption within their offices.
Ramos said he wanted all departments to list measures they had undertaken to curb corruption. The measures were termed as prevention, prosecution and rehabilitation.
All departments were expected to file the report by the 10th of each month, a government statement said.
Concern over this issue has risen recently after Transparency International, a Berlin-based organisation, ranked the Philippines the 11th most corrupt country in the world.

"As part of this administration's programme of energising the bureaucracy and making public service more effective and efficient, I expect your departments and agencies to vigorously pursue this campaign without let-up," Ramos said.

Since 1992, the government has filed graft cases against 24 officials of the Bureau of Internal Revenues, 23 prosecutors, 436 rank-and-file employees, and six postmasters for dishonesty and grave misconduct.
Ramos has himself dismissed two high-ranking officials over anomalous deals.
